cards.text: Daniel's on the bank of the Tigris River, and the one sent to him is explaining what will happen to Daniel's people. He starts with Persia: three more kings will arise, and then a fourth. Friend, that's a LOT of crowns, so tie your apron tight.

cards.question: Persia gets three more kings, and then a fourth. What sets the fourth king apart?

answers.text: He's far richer than all the others
He rules longer than all the others
He's wiser than all the others

cards.question: With all that wealth, the fourth king of Persia stirs up everyone against the kingdom of ___.

cards.text: Then a mighty king arises who rules with great authority and does as he pleases. Friend, I can't even get my OVEN TIMER to do as I please.

cards.question: As soon as the mighty king is established, what happens to his kingdom?

answers.text: It's broken up toward the four winds
It stays whole for many generations
It grows to twice its size

cards.question: The mighty king's kingdom goes to his descendants.

cards.text: It doesn't keep his authority either, because it's uprooted and given to others. Friend, I KNOW that feeling: one day there's a shiny new stamper sitting in my spot on the Millers' counter.
Now meet the king of the South. He grows strong, but somebody close to him is about to pass him up.

cards.question: The king of the South grows strong. Who grows even stronger and rules his own kingdom with great authority?

cards.text: After some years an alliance forms, and the daughter of the king of the South goes to the king of the North to seal the agreement. That's our first look at the king of the North, and trust me, friend, you're gonna see a LOT of him.

cards.question: The daughter of the king of the South keeps her position of power.

cards.text: She's given up, along with her royal escort, her father and the one who supported her. But one from her family line rises up in his place.

cards.question: One from the daughter's family line rises up. What does he do?

answers.text: He enters the North's fortress and prevails
He makes peace with the king of the North
He flees from the king of the North

cards.question: He even takes the North's ___ captive to ___, along with their metal images and their precious vessels of silver and gold.

cards.text: For some years he stays away from the king of the North, who invades the South's realm and then goes home. Back and forth, back and forth, like two coworkers fighting over the office thermostat.

cards.question: The sons of the king of the North put together a great army that sweeps through like a flood.

cards.text: That flood carries the battle as far as his fortress. Now it's the king of the South's move.

cards.question: The North's army has pushed as far as the fortress. What does the king of the South do?

answers.text: He marches out in a rage to fight
He hides inside his fortress walls
He sends gold to buy peace

cards.question: The large army the king of the North raises is delivered into the hand of the king of the South.

cards.text: When the army is carried off, the king of the South gets proud in heart and casts down tens of thousands. But he will not triumph, and friend, I know that move: I bragged about ONE perfect cookie, and the next batch came out looking like a smudge.
Round two: after some years, the king of the North advances with a great army and many supplies. MANY supplies, friend, this is the guy who packs four suitcases for a weekend trip.

cards.question: How does the king of the North's new army compare to the army he lost to the South?

answers.text: It's the same size as the first

cards.text: In those times, many rise up against the king of the South. Meanwhile, violent ones among Daniel's own people exalt themselves in fulfillment of the vision.

cards.question: The violent ones among Daniel's own people exalt themselves, but they will ___.

cards.text: Then the king of the North builds a siege ramp and captures a fortified city. He's not knocking, friend, he's building himself a DRIVEWAY.

cards.question: The king of the North just captured a fortified city. How do the forces of the South hold up?

answers.text: Not even their best troops can resist
They hold the walls for many years
They drive the North back home

cards.text: The invader does as he pleases, and no one stands against him. He establishes himself in the Beautiful Land, with destruction in his hand.

cards.question: The king of the North comes with the strength of his whole kingdom and reaches an agreement with the king of the South. What does he give him?
The king of the North gives the daughter in marriage in order to overthrow the kingdom, and his plan succeeds.

cards.text: Then he turns his face to the coastlands and captures many of them. This man is on a ROLL, friend.

cards.question: In the coastlands, who puts an end to the king of the North's reproach and turns it back upon him?

cards.text: After this, he turns back toward the fortresses of his own land.

cards.question: The king of the North rules safely from his own fortresses for many more years.

cards.text: Instead he stumbles and falls and is no more. In his place, one arises who sends out a tax collector for the glory of the kingdom, and I bet that's NOT the parade anybody was hoping for.

cards.question: Within a few days, the king who sent out the tax collector is destroyed in battle.

cards.text: Then a despicable person arises, and royal honors will not be given to him. When your introduction is DESPICABLE, friend, you already know you're not the hero.

cards.question: Royal honors won't be given to the despicable person. So how does he get the kingdom?

answers.text: He seizes it by intrigue in a time of peace
He wins it in a great battle at sea
He inherits it from his own father

cards.text: Then a flood of forces is swept away before him and destroyed, along with a prince of the covenant.

cards.question: After an alliance is made with the despicable person, he acts honestly.

cards.text: He rises to power with only a few people, then in a time of peace invades the richest provinces. He does what his fathers and forefathers never did, and friend, that is NOT a compliment.

cards.question: The despicable person comes away with plunder, loot and wealth. What does he do with it?

answers.text: He lavishes it on his followers
He hides it away in his strongholds
He sends it as tribute to the South

cards.text: Then with a large army, he stirs up his power and his courage against the king of the South, who mobilizes a very large and powerful army. Apparently NOBODY in this vision owns a small army.

cards.question: The king of the South has a very large and powerful army. What can't he withstand?

answers.text: A sickness spreading through his camp
A storm that wrecks his ships

cards.question: The people who seek to destroy the king of the South are those who eat from his provisions.

cards.text: His army is swept away, and many fall slain. Then the two kings, hearts bent on evil, sit at the same table and speak lies.

cards.question: The lies the two kings tell at the same table get them what they want.
The king of the North returns to his land with great wealth, but his heart is set against the holy ___.

cards.text: So he does damage and returns to his own land. Then at the appointed time he invades the South again, but this time will not be like the first.

cards.question: This invasion of the South isn't like the first one. What comes against the king of the North?
When the king of the North loses heart and turns back, he shows favor to those who forsake the holy covenant.

cards.text: His forces rise up and desecrate the temple fortress. They abolish the daily sacrifice and set up the abomination of desolation.

cards.question: With flattery he corrupts those who violate the covenant, but the people who know their God will firmly ___ him.

cards.text: Those with insight instruct many, though for a time they fall by sword or flame, or are captured or plundered. When they fall, they're granted a little help, but many join them insincerely.

cards.question: Some of the wise will fall. Why does the messenger say it happens?

answers.text: So they may be refined and purified
So their enemies may be put to shame
So the king of the North may lose heart

cards.text: Refined, purified and made spotless until the time of the end, which will still come at the appointed time. And that's where we leave it for now, friend, because this vision is NOT done talking.
